Get started with FunMel

Mitra Ghotbi

Source: vignettes/FunMel.Rmd
FunMel.Rmd

What FunMel measures

FunMel measures colour, shape and image-darkness profiles of approximately round Zymoseptoria tritici colonies around a central fungus. It separates central fungal tissue and peripheral hyphal growth from target-colony masks. The measured outlines can be irregular. These are image-based tissue candidates, not species identifications or an inhibition zone.

Melanization index is MI = 100 - CIELAB L*: larger values indicate darker pixels. It is a proxy, not a direct measurement of melanin concentration. Imaging conditions, calibration and segmentation affect the result.

The standard workflow is prepare, run, finish. No approval columns need to be edited. Review reminders inform users without interrupting valid runs. Check experimental assignments before analysis and masks, calibration and warnings before interpreting results.

Installation 

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel")
library(FunMel)

Restart R before updating a loaded package. R >= 4.1 and a source compilation toolchain are required: Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS, matching Rtools on Windows, or R development tools and ImageMagick development libraries on Linux. To install the local vignette:

remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel", build_vignettes=TRUE,
                        dependencies=TRUE)
vignette("FunMel", package="FunMel")

A first simulated plate

This example needs no photographs or metadata editing. Simulation tests computational behavior; it does not validate biological accuracy on real images.

sim <- simulate_plate(width=400, height=400, seed=1)
x <- analyze_plate(sim$image, n_spots=3, spot_radius_mm=0.4,
                   n_boot=20, verbose=FALSE)
x$colonies[, c("colony_id", "detected", "MI_min", "MI_mean", "MI_max")]
#>   colony_id detected   MI_min  MI_mean   MI_max
#> 1        TL     TRUE 35.90361 48.81529 80.12348
#> 2        TR     TRUE 32.06814 52.99384 79.60242
#> 3        BR     TRUE 39.44803 57.17307 79.25676
#> 4        BL     TRUE 24.59659 41.43033 80.26735
plot_qc(x)

Review the colony outlines and central fungal/hyphal regions. For an actual control photograph, set layout=plate_layout(centre="none") in analyze_plate(). The default confrontation layout has a central fungus and four target colonies.

Follow the real 14-day photographs: step by step

Eight unchanged original photographs are included. They form two matching sets, each with one control and three independent confrontation plates; four target colonies are measured within each plate. No separate download is needed.

Set Control Confrontation photographs
A60_2_14_days 2026_10_02_99_41.JPG 38.JPG, 39.JPG, 40.JPG, with the same filename prefix
B20_2_14_days 2026_10_02_99_45.JPG 42.JPG, 43.JPG, 44.JPG, with the same filename prefix

These folder-derived labels are supplied for teaching. Verify their biological meaning and assignments against laboratory records. The source field hm83 is retained without inferring its biological role. Unrecorded strain/medium fields remain blank. No user approval switch is needed to run the example.

Step 1. Prepare the project once 

library(FunMel)
photos14 <- system.file("extdata", "14-days", package="FunMel")
stopifnot(nzchar(photos14))
project14 <- prepare_experiment(photos14, "FunMel_14_day_project")
project14$metadata_file

The combined metadata is read automatically. The printed path identifies the project copy of plate_metadata.csv. Check treatment labels, controls, matching set_id, centre_model, day and replicate labels. Only edit missing or incorrect experimental information. There are no approval flags to change. Each control appears once and shares a set with its three treatment plates. Use a new project folder only for a genuinely new project; do not recreate a project merely to finalize saved results.

Step 2. Measure all eight photographs

Set the verified outer dish diameter directly. The value 90 below is illustrative, not an experimentally verified measurement of these photographs. All images in one run use the same scale; analyze different dish sizes separately.

dish_mm <- 90 # Replace with the verified outer dish diameter (mm).
result14 <- run_experiment(
  project14, dish_diameter_mm=dish_mm, max_dim=1200,
  n_spots=5, spot_radius_mm=0.4
)
result14$analysis_status
result14$failed
stopifnot(nrow(result14$failed)==0L)

Processing saves image_analysis.rds, measurement CSVs and QC PNGs. A successful run reports analysis_status="complete" and an empty failed table. Partial or failed runs save error reports and must be corrected before finalization. No review-flag editing is required.

Whole-colony measurements use eligible interior pixels after excluding the rim and saturated/specular pixels. Five circular spots per colony are requested here as additional spatial samples. Omit n_spots and spot_radius_mm if only whole-colony measurements are needed. Keep settings consistent across plates.

Step 3. Inspect the image QC

Open the folder printed by:

project14$qc_dir

Check every PNG for target-colony boundaries, separation of central fungal tissue and hyphae, spot locations, scale, shadows, illumination and measurement warnings. Correct unsuitable measurements or photographs before interpretation. The package provides reminders; it does not wait for a manual approval record.

Illumination correction is requested by default but can be withheld when fitted gains saturate. Inspect flat_field_applied and flat_field_status in the plate table. Withholding does not mean the illumination is adequate. A treatment/control ratio cannot be assumed to cancel lighting or exposure differences. Rephotograph under consistent conditions when needed.

Step 4. Calculate coefficients and export the figure 

reviewed14 <- finish_experiment(project14)
reviewed14$melanization_coefficient
reviewed14$assessment$status
list.files(project14$project_dir)

Finalization reads saved measurements and metadata automatically; no image reprocessing or FALSE-to-TRUE edits are needed. Informative reminders and image QC warnings do not block the default workflow. They do not establish biological validation or automatically approve images.

Each treatment uses only its own set’s control. This example has one control per set, so coefficients and the figure are descriptive; the built-in replicated-cell inference guard does not permit significance tests. Four target colonies and five spots within each colony do not create additional independent plate replicates. Between-treatment comparisons can also remain confounded with batch here.

File Contents
colonies.csv Whole-colony measurements and spot summaries
spots.csv Individual spot locations and measurements
plates.csv Plate summaries, illumination status and warnings
profiles.csv Edge-to-centre measurements
metadata_used.csv Full experimental metadata, including custom columns
melanization_coefficient.csv Own-set treatment/control ratios
per_plate_coefficients.csv Plate ratios using their own matched control means
reviewed_analysis.rds Finalized results; the filename does not certify review
treatment_comparison.pdf/.svg/.png Vector and 600-dpi comparison figure
treatment_comparison_statistics.csv Means, SDs, counts and descriptive statistics
qc_review_status.csv Recorded image-review status; no default approval requirement

The comparison figure distinguishes control squares, coloured treatment circles and mean diamonds. Bars and printed plus/minus values show one between-plate SD, not confidence intervals. SD is unavailable for a single control. Ratio SD conditions on the shared control mean and omits its uncertainty.

Step 5. Resume later without repeating image analysis 

library(FunMel)
project14 <- readRDS(file.choose()) # Select this project's project.rds.
reviewed14 <- finish_experiment(project14)

A relative path such as FunMel_14_day_project/project.rds works only when the working directory contains that folder. A file chooser avoids guessing the working directory. Keep the project CSV and saved results available locally.

The companion script examples/walkthrough_14_days.R follows these same steps. Precomputed tables in extdata/14_day_example use an illustrative 90-mm scale, max_dim=1200, five 0.4-mm-radius spots and n_boot=20; see their provenance. They are not ground truth or high-precision bootstrap uncertainty estimates.

Analyze a photograph folder or nested ZIP 

project <- prepare_experiment(file.choose(), "FunMel_project")
# Check the printed metadata; correct only missing or inaccurate labels.
result <- run_experiment(project, dish_diameter_mm=90,
                         n_spots=5, spot_radius_mm=0.4)
result$failed
# Inspect QC, then calculate/export using saved measurements:
reviewed <- finish_experiment(project)

Replace 90 with the actual outer dish diameter. Nested folders such as day8/batch1/control/ and day8/batch1/fungus_A/ suggest matching groups. Only explicit control folder labels are recognized by default; use control_folders="C" only when that label actually denotes control. A ZIP can contain one combined plate_metadata.csv; otherwise pass a combined metadata table explicitly through metadata=. Ambiguous file names cannot establish treatments or decide which control belongs to which experiment.

Each metadata row represents an independent plate. Preserve file provenance and unique plate IDs. Enter each control once within its own matching set. Record day, medium and strain explicitly; once recorded, each context must be complete and constant within a set. Different contexts are finalized separately into indexed folders, with context_index.csv describing the outputs. Repeated images of the same plate are not independent biological replicates.

Coefficients and statistical assessment

A plate’s MI is the equally weighted mean of its target-colony MI_mean values. The matched coefficient is the mean of treatment plate MI values divided by the mean of control plate MI values within the same set. Overall treatment summaries weight set-specific ratios equally rather than pooling all controls. Values above 1 mean a darker treatment mean, not a fold change in pigment concentration.

With adequate independent plate replication, assess_experiment() uses lme4/lmerTest plate-level random effects, matched-set contrasts and Holm adjustment. The explicit method="plate_means" alternative works on independent plate means. Check model assumptions, convergence, singularity, experimental coverage and potential confounding; passing a computational guard does not prove that a sample size or model is scientifically adequate.

The following synthetic experiment illustrates a comparison with replicated controls. Its numbers are simulated, not results from the photographs.

demo <- example_experiment(seed=42)
plot_treatment_comparison(demo)

Whole-colony versus optional spot measurements

MI_min, MI_mean and MI_max summarize eligible whole-colony pixels. spots.csv stores each measured circular ROI’s location, radius and pixel-level MI summaries. MI_spot_mean/min/max are the mean, minimum and maximum of individual spot means. These differ from whole-colony pixel extrema and are not confidence intervals.

Spots are placed with a deterministic spatial-spread algorithm, not random sampling. They must be non-overlapping and entirely inside usable target tissue. The bounded greedy search may fail to fit all requested spots even when another packing exists. Check n_spots_measured and spot_status; incomplete spot summaries are unavailable rather than filled with invented values.

Default coefficients and assessment use whole-colony MI. A study that prespecifies a consistently applied spot-based descriptive response can use:

spot_coefficients <- melanization_coefficient(reviewed14, response="MI_spot_mean")

Do not test individual spots, pixels or within-plate colonies as independent biological replicates. Keep response definitions clear when reporting results.

Metadata and recovery

Custom metadata names and values are retained. The complete table is stored in result$metadata and metadata_used.csv. Conflicts with measured column names receive a metadata_ prefix only in measurement tables; original names remain in the full metadata. No metadata approval column is generated or required. An optional recorded qc_pass field is reset for a new image run, but never needs editing for the standard workflow.

Problem Action
Missing treatment or set labels Complete the actual experimental assignments; folder suggestions are not proof
Missing relevant control Supply the correct control in the same matching set; do not borrow another batch’s control
Missing metadata CSV Restore the edited CSV or correct its recorded path; do not recreate the project
Cloud file unavailable Download the CSV and photographs locally
Invalid diameter Set a finite positive numeric diameter directly; do not paste code into a prompt
Failed images Inspect result$failed, correct errors and rerun before finalization
Spots do not fit Inspect status and choose consistent settings across compared plates
Unconfirmed image QC warning Review masks, calibration and warnings; default computation continues without flag edits
Changed image layout Reanalyze because saved masks used different settings
Descriptive-only assessment Check independent plate replication and design; do not invent significance tests

Advanced users can explicitly opt into a stricter image-QC policy through require_qc=TRUE. It is never enabled by the standard workflow and is unrelated to metadata approval. Do not select strict mode unless that review policy is intended.

Methods and further examples

The image workflow detects a dish boundary, fits an agar background model, applies a guarded illumination correction when usable, separates colour/texture regions with layout initialization and watershed-based separation, and measures eligible target pixels. Image masks and calibration need independent review; classification does not establish species identity or quantify melanin chemistry.

The separate guides/FunMel_overview.md explains properties, functions, algorithms and uses alongside ImageJ/Fiji. Manual ROI tools remain valuable for difficult boundaries; no universal accuracy or speed advantage is claimed.

source(system.file("examples","01_image_quickstart.R",package="FunMel"))
source(system.file("examples","02_coefficient_arithmetic.R",package="FunMel"))
